links.outcome: Readability of LLM responses relative to recommended sixth-grade reading level
links.effect: All five models exceeded commonly recommended sixth-grade readability thresholds; readability differences between models were more pronounced than informational-quality differences.
links.quote: Readability differences were more pronounced, and all models exceeded commonly recommended sixth-grade readability thresholds.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of LLM patient education responses (readability indices)
links.effect: All models exceeded recommended sixth-grade readability thresholds across six readability indices, indicating suboptimal readability for patients.
links.quote: Readability differences were more pronounced, and all models exceeded commonly recommended sixth-grade readability thresholds.

links.outcome: Visible attribution and verifiability cues (JAMA benchmark) in default LLM outputs
links.effect: JAMA scores uniformly low (means 0.00-0.25; medians 0), indicating sparse visible attribution and limited verifiability cues.
links.quote: JAMA scores were uniformly low (means, 0.00-0.25; medians, 0), indicating sparse visible attribution and limited verifiability cues in default outputs.

screen.reason: Evaluates public LLM baseline responses to patient-facing clinical questions regarding quality, verifiability, and readability without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
